Subject: Production burst — sustained 429s and latency spike

SoojIN,

We started seeing a major spike in 429s and p95 latency on our ingest route at ~08:30 PT and it's been consistently impacting our customers. We've attached a log bundle and a short replay showing the traffic pattern — it looks like something in Redwood's quota/burst interaction is preventing our short bursts from succeeding.

Impact: 40% of our requests into /v1/generate are returning 429, overall latency > 3s p95. This is hitting our billing customers and our execs are asking for immediate mitigation.

Can you confirm whether there's an active throttling policy or burst credit exhaustion on your end? We need either a temporary override or a quick rollback to the previous policy.

Jordan Harris
Director of Platform
FluxScale

Attachments: fluxscale-support-logbundle-20290520.zip (logs, 4MB); replay-08-30.har

- If you can provide a tight timestamp window of ~1 minute where you see the first surge, that helps correlate to our internal metrics.

I'll follow up within 30 mins with either a mitigation (temporary burst credit top-up / policy override) or a plan and ETA. Apologies for the disruption — we understand the executive pressure.

— Soojin

Subject: Fwd: Production burst — sustained 429s and latency spike

Marissa / Karthik / Monica — escalating to leadership + infra. FluxScale (strategic enterprise customer, deal FS-ENTERPRISE-2029-07) is hitting sustained 429s and latency; they report it's related to our quota/burst behavior. They already provided a log bundle.

Key facts:
- Customer impact: 40% 429s on /v1/generate, p95 >3s
- Time window: starts ~08:30 PT, ongoing
- Likely vector: hyperburst traffic pattern (many short high-concurrency bursts) hitting a mismatch between quota windows and burst credit accounting.

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik — can you have infra confirm whether there was a policy change or rollout to rate/burst code around 08:00–09:00 PT? Also check whether the recent change to burst-credit persistence (PR #1542) could be double-counting credits across routes.
2) Monica — please engage SRE to prepare a temporary override (increase burst allowance for FluxScale tenant) and a fail-open routing rule that would route to a compatible model variant if we detect >30% 429s in 5m.
3) Marissa — this should be flagged to Execs (FluxScale execs are on the thread). If you want me to draft the exec summary, I will.

I've attached the customer's bundle to this thread and included links to the Jira and Drive folder. Time is sensitive — they indicated exec-level asks.

— Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the fast escalation, Soojin. Karthik / Monica — prioritize. This is high-severity because FluxScale is in an active sales + renewal cycle and execs are watching. Please do the following right away:

- Karthik: snapshot the policy state and confirm whether any quota/burst policy rollouts touched tenant-scoped accounting in the 08:00–09:00 window. If a rollout happened, prepare an immediate rollback plan and a target ETA (preferably <2 hours).
- Monica: apply a tenant-level temporary burst top-up of +200% for FluxScale and enable the fail-open routing for their tenant only. Notify me once done.
- Soojin: prepare a concise external note to Jordan/Priya telling them the mitigation and a visible ETA for a root cause update. Keep it short and set expectations (we will follow with RCA within 48 hours).

I will loop in VP Ops if we see rollback required; keep me posted.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Harris <jharris@fluxscale.com>, Priya Anand <priya.anand@fluxscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Action taken: temporary burst top-up + mitigation steps (short update)

Jordan / Priya — quick update following our escalation: 

1) We applied a tenant-specific burst top-up (+200% credits) at 14:10 PT and enabled a fail-open routing rule for FluxScale at 14:15 PT.
2) After the top-up we observed 429 rate drop from ~40% to <3% within 10 minutes; p95 latency moved back to ~350ms.
3) Preliminary root-cause: a recent change to burst-credit persistence (PR #1542) caused certain short-lived bursts to consume credits across sibling routes instead of being isolated per route; that interaction accelerated credit exhaustion for high-concurrency, short-duration workloads. Karthik's team has a rollback candidate and will run a canary prior to full rollback.

Next steps / ETA:
- Short term (now): mitigation applied and customer traffic stabilized.
- Mid term (by EOD): engineering will run a canary rollback and validate with the customer's replay traffic.
- RCA report (48 hours): full timeline, code PRs, and compensating controls (policy tests + proactive alerts).

We've attached the support log bundle and the exported burst-policy config. Apologies again — we know execs were notified; I'm happy to join a sync if you want real-time updates.

Regards,
SoojIN Lee | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: fluxscale-support-logbundle-20290520.zip; burst-policy-config-exports.txt
